nodes.description: Heterozygous missense, in-frame deletion or splice-site variants clustered in the coiled-coil domain of CARD14 (CARMA2), the skin-restricted member of the CARMA scaffold family. The variants disrupt the autoinhibitory contact between the linker region and the CARD/coiled-coil domains, so that the mutant scaffold signals without an upstream stimulus. Gain of function is demonstrated biochemically for the psoriasis alleles p.Glu138Ala and p.Gly117Ser (the latter also a PRP allele) and inferred for the other PRP alleles from their position in the same domain and the NF-kappaB activation seen in patient skin.

nodes.description: The first mouse carrying a PRP-causing human allele. Homozygotes develop generalized scaling, hair-follicle dilatation and plugging, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis, markedly increased transepidermal water loss, IL-36/inflammasome and IL-17-axis activation in the outer root sheath and interfollicular epidermis, and high neonatal mortality; anti-IL-17A improves inflammation but not barrier function. nodes.description: Heterozygous knock-in of a psoriasis-associated gain-of-function allele from the same coiled-coil region. nodes.description: Alternating vertical and horizontal orthokeratosis and parakeratosis, acanthosis without acantholysis, dilated papillary vessels and, in some biopsies, follicular plugging; the pattern favours PRP over psoriasis and was found consistently in biopsies from genotyped patients.

nodes.description: Mutant CARD14 constitutively associates with BCL10 and the paracaspase MALT1 to form a CBM-type signalosome in keratinocytes, the counterpart of the CARD11-BCL10-MALT1 complex formed in lymphocytes after antigen-receptor stimulation. The complex engages IKK and also activates MALT1 protease activity, which cleaves negative regulators of NF-kappaB; MALT1 deficiency or inhibition blunts mutant CARD14 signalling in keratinocytes and in mice.

evidence.snippet: Notable is the near complete response to ustekinumab in 5 of 6 subjects treated and partial response in the sixth (subject 5), who had the most severe phenotype and was also notably the heaviest and thus may have required a higher dosage.

evidence.reference_title: Beneficial effect of ustekinumab in familial pityriasis rubra pilaris with a new missense mutation in CARD14.
evidence.snippet: Ustekinumab, at a dose of 45 mg every 12 weeks, brought about a significant physical and emotional improvement in both the mother and son within a few days of the initial dose, which was sustained on maintenance dosing.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of a pathogenic CARD14 mutation in a 70-year-old woman with pityriasis rubra pilaris: when genetic diagnosis influences choice of treatment strategy.
evidence.snippet: Therapy with ustekinumab was initiated with remarkable effect, which improved the patient's quality of life significantly.

evidence.reference_title: Treatment Options for Juvenile Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris.
evidence.snippet: Ustekinumab, in particular, is emerging as a first-line agent for patients with pityriasis rubra pilaris with CARD14 gene variations.
